articles.title: 巴慕达推出 AI 个性化电台“Good Morning Radio”，可根据用户生活习惯与兴趣生成 10 分钟每日播客
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，巴慕达（BALMUDA）宣布推出 AI 个性化电台服务 BALMUDA Good Morning Radio，计划于 2026 年 11 月 2 日起面向旗下 The Clock 时钟用户开放 Beta 测试版，没有购买时钟的用户也可通过巴慕达 BALMUDA Connect 应用申请测试（限量 1000 名）。据巴慕达介绍，与传统广播及播客面向大量用户提供同一节目不同，Good Morning Radio 引入了 AI 技术，可以根据用户的生活习惯与兴趣生成约 10 分钟的每日电台音频，内容不仅涵盖新闻、天气等时事资讯，还会围绕用户感兴趣的话题展开，帮助用户发现新的旅行目的地、美食、音乐、电影及书籍等内容。巴慕达表示，该服务将品牌自身的内容策划与节目导演能力，与 AI 的内容制作能力相结合，既保留品牌所注重的感性与创意，也利用 AI 提升内容制作效率。官方特别强调，希望通过电台这种媒介保留意料之外的发现，让用户在获取必要信息的同时，也能接触到原本没有主动寻找的新话题。在使用方式上，The Clock 用户可通过设备和巴慕达 BALMUDA Connect 应用收听节目。设备连接 Wi-Fi 后，每天早晨会自动同步新一期节目，用户只需按下机身顶部的旋钮，即可开始收听当天约 10 分钟的专属电台。通过应用收听则无需直接操作时钟设备。对于尚未购买 The Clock 的用户，巴慕达也开放了限额 1000 人的 Beta 体验申请（点此访问）。申请截止日期为 11 月 3 日，当选结果预计于 11 月 9 日公布，获选用户可通过 BALMUDA Connect 应用输入邀请码体验服务。

articles.title: 美国国土安全部遭黑客入侵，逾 4 万名员工敏感资料外泄
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，据路透社报道，当地时间 28 日，泄密网站、致力于推动数据透明的非营利组织 Distributed Denial of Secrets 公布了超过 4 万名美国国土安全部员工的资料，其中涉及从事监控、人力情报等敏感工作的人员。美国国土安全部回应说，获悉可能发生数据泄露后，正积极采取措施，争取尽快妥善处理。国土安全部将确保员工受到适当保护，并在掌握更多信息后向公众通报。泄露资料由一个自称 Department of Peace（IT之家注：下称“和平部”）的组织获取。这也是过去一个月内第三起引发广泛关注的美国政府重大数据泄露事件。今年 9 月，黑客组织 ShinyHunters 声称窃取了美国联邦调查局的大量数据，包括数千名员工的敏感岗位信息和医疗资料。上周，美国国防部也因数百万名现役及曾服役军人资料泄露而遭到集体诉讼。此次泄露的数据涉及国土安全部多个下属机构，涵盖移民与海关执法局、海关与边境保护局、国土安全调查局、网络安全和基础设施安全局等，内容则包含了员工姓名、电话号码和电子邮箱地址。泄露资料还包含员工职务及电子邮件群组信息，从中可以辨认出哪些执法人员负责特别行动、监控、计算机取证和卧底任务。“和平部”未立即回应置评请求，仅在随泄露资料发布的声明中提到：“国土安全部员工掌握着我们的信息，所以我们掌握他们的信息才公平。这些数据有助于减少国土安全部今后造成的伤害，支持为此采取的一切行动。”今年 3 月，“和平部”曾宣称入侵了国土安全部系统，并公布了该部门与外部供应商签订的合同文件。通过比对征信机构记录和暗网情报平台 District 4 Labs 收录的泄露数据，路透社确认了其中 6 名国土安全部员工的个人信息吻合。路透社还直接联系了 3 名国土安全部员工，核实了他们的电话号码等信息。其中一人表示，自己此前根本不知道发生过数据泄露。部分泄露资料与国土安全部员工在领英上公开的信息一致，也有资料涉及该部门未公开的内部组织架构，以及此前不为外界所知的项目或行动。

articles.title: 中汽学会发布 2027 年度中国汽车十大技术趋势，含 400Wh/kg 级固态电池进入中试阶段等
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，10 月 28 日下午，第三十三届中国汽车工程学会年会开幕式暨全体大会在苏州举行。中国汽车工程学会副秘书长、国汽战略院执行院长郑亚莉在会上发布《2027 年度中国汽车十大技术趋势》。据介绍，十大趋势主要聚焦性能与成本重大突破、新量产落地、应用规模显著提升三大方向，为产业前瞻布局、协同创新和创新资源配置提供了重要参考。IT之家附十大技术趋势如下：单体能量密度 400Wh/kg 级的固态电池进入中试阶段高安全等级 RISC-V 汽车 MCU 迎来量产元年融合型整车运动控制技术应用将加速普及V2G 日均可提供反向灵活调节能力达百万级千瓦镁合金一体化成形车身大铸件将实现小规模应用高级别自动驾驶卡车编队迈入千辆级示范运营分布式轮毂驱动工程化验证全面提速主流量产车型座舱端侧模型部署参数突破 14B网联辅助驾驶从示范验证走向小批量前装金属 3D 打印技术将在材料、设计、效率等方面协同突破▲ 图源中国汽车工程学会

articles.title: 全新 Bose 有线消噪耳塞国行上市：IPX4 防水、USB-C 接口，699 元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，全新 Bose 有线消噪耳塞（Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds）国行版本今日上市，售价 699 元。这款耳机拥有经典黑、晨雾白，以及限量款沁凉薄荷三种配色可选；通过 USB-C 接口直连设备供电，即插即用；搭载 Bose 标志性的 QuietControl 降噪技术，支持在安静模式、通透模式与降噪关闭三档之间自由切换。这款耳机兼容无损音频播放，具备 IPX4 防水等级，提供 3 种尺寸耳塞头与 2 种尺寸耳翼可自由选配，产品随附专属便携收纳包。IT之家附这款耳机主要卖点：京东博士（BOSE）有线消噪耳塞 沁凉薄荷（限量款）券后 699 元领 5 元券京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，迈从宣布旗下 R9 轻量化零压电竞头戴耳机“白紫”“黑金”两款配色现已正式发售，该耳机主打“迈从全自研苍穹方案”“THX 空间音效”，定价为 299 元，首发价 249.2 元。京东迈从 R9 头戴式耳机券后 249.2 元领 20 元券该耳机提供白紫、黑金、黑色、粉色和白蓝多种配色，整体重量约 235 g。其搭载天羽悬浮工学头梁，内置航空级琴钢线骨架，配合柔韧头带提升贴合度。耳罩部分采用太空透气记忆棉与蛋白皮层，并结合透气网布材质。耳机骨轴采用 90° 旋翼设计，机身支持多维无极调节，可直接通过实体按键进行控制。该耳机配备 53 mm 三层高分子复合振膜单元与独立腔体，支持 THX 空间音效与迈从自研苍穹方案，搭配可插拔的 360° 全指向 AI 降噪麦克风，耳机应用 MCHOSE TOPSPEED WIRELESS 无线技术，响应延迟约 15 ms。耳机内置 1050 mAh 容量电池，在满电状态下的续航时间可达约 150 小时。IT之家附产品参数：京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 山灵预热“星光 Celesta”银铜耳机升级线：主打均衡百搭，1498 元明日发售
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，山灵发文，预热旗下「星光 Celesta」银铜耳机升级线将于明天发售，该产品由山灵与香港瞬声联合打造，主打均衡百搭与高频通透感，零售价 1598 元，首发价 1498 元。该升级线的线身使用美国 SoftFlex 医疗级外皮，带有若隐若现的彩色光点，呼应「星光」命名。据官方介绍，该升级线旨在“提升基础素质、均衡百搭”，其线材采用高密度同轴屏蔽结构，主线芯为 4N 长结晶纯银，负极采用加粗长晶铜镀银工艺，补足低频动态与下潜。整体作用是“理顺声场、抚平毛刺、保留耳机原有风味”。

articles.title: 甲骨文公布“扭亏为盈”计划，力图安抚投资者担忧情绪
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，据路透社报道，当地时间 28 日，甲骨文披露，随着云计算业务扩张，资本开支预计将在 2027 和 2028 财年达到高峰，并承诺截至 2030 财年，为 AI 业务新增的融资不超过 200 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,336.11 亿元人民币）。甲骨文希望借此缓解投资者对资金需求不断膨胀的担忧。投资者担心，甲骨文为大举建设数据中心，需要持续从外部筹集巨额资金。受业绩预测提振，甲骨文股价大涨超过 12%，其他云计算公司股价也随之上涨。甲骨文 CFO 希拉里 · 麦克斯顿在投资者日活动上透露，公司预计 2028 财年下半年实现自由现金流转正，2029 财年自由现金流超过 300 亿美元（现汇率约合 2,004.16 亿元人民币），资本开支也将在当年回落。甲骨文的 AI 基础设施投资成本不断攀升，成为市场关注的焦点。与微软、亚马逊等云计算巨头相比，甲骨文缺乏雄厚的营收基础，业务还高度依赖尚未盈利的 OpenAI。与 OpenAI 的合作让甲骨文新增了数千亿美元的云计算订单，但要履行这些合同，就必须建设大量数据中心及其他 AI 基础设施，迫使公司高度依赖借债和发行股票筹资。甲骨文透露，通过供应商融资、由客户自行提供硬件以及预收客户款项等方式，公司有望在自由现金流转正前减少前期资金投入。按照甲骨文的预测，公司从 2029 财年起无需再依靠外部融资支持增长，当年净债务与年度核心利润之比也将降至 3.5 倍以下。今年早些时候，甲骨文曾宣布计划在 2027 财年通过债务和股权融资筹集 400 亿美元（现汇率约合 2,672.22 亿元人民币），其中 200 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,336.11 亿元人民币）的股票发行已在第一季度完成。截至 8 月 31 日，甲骨文的应付票据及其他借款总额达到 1,253.4 亿美元（现汇率约合 8,373.39 亿元人民币），持有现金及现金等价物约 363.7 亿美元（现汇率约合 2,429.71 亿元人民币）。甲骨文预计 2030 财年营收超过 2,250 亿美元（现汇率约合 1.5 万亿元人民币），调整后营业利润率超过 40%，调整后每股收益超过 21 美元（现汇率约合 140.3 元人民币）。同时，公司维持 2027 财年营收超过 900 亿美元（现汇率约合 6,012.48 亿元人民币）、调整后每股收益 8.10 美元（现汇率约合 54.1 元人民币）的预测。

articles.title: 首发 Lofic HDR 4.0、2X 焦段也支持：思特威推出 5000 万像素 1/1.28 英寸 CMOS SC5D8XS
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，思特威今日宣布，正式推出业界首颗同时支持 1X 和 2X 焦段 LOFIC 的 5000 万像素超高动态范围手机应用图像传感器 ——SC5D8XS。基于 Lofic HDR 4.0 技术，SC5D8XS 首次在 2X 焦段实现 LOFIC 功能，支持 2X 焦段下的 LOFIC 高动态拍摄：1X 焦段动态范围最高可达 110dB，2X 焦段动态范围亦可达 100dB。据介绍，针对视频录制中常见的运动伪影问题，思特威 Lofic HDR 4.0 技术基于单次曝光内的三帧融合实现，能够有效抑制运动拖影，使运动主体边缘更锐利清晰，从而实现明暗有致、清晰无拖影的高质量视频效果。SC5D8XS 支持 Lofic HDR 4.0 模式下 4K 60fps 的高动态范围高帧率视频录制，并支持 PixGain HDR 模式下 4K 120fps 超高帧率视频录制。在 LOFIC 模式下，SC5D8XS 针对不同焦段采用差异化对焦策略：1X 焦段支持 6% 部分像素相位检测对焦，在保障对焦性能的同时降低运行功耗；2X 焦段实现 100% 全像素对焦，带来更快速、更准确的自动对焦表现。SC5D8XS 在普通模式下搭载思特威 AllPix ADAF 与 Sparse PDAF 技术，支持 100% 全像素对焦与 6% 部分像素相位检测对焦两种自适应快速对焦模式，可根据光线条件灵活切换。SC5D8XS 采用 22nm Stack 先进工艺制程，并通过精细化的功耗调优显著降低功耗。在 Lofic HDR 4.0 高清视频模式下，SC5D8XS 的功耗约 550mW，较前代产品降低约 18%；在常规工作模式下，SC5D8XS 的功耗为 200mW。目前，SC5D8XS 已实现量产，IT之家附详细参数如下：

articles.title: Tencent’s Cloud Boss Plays Long Game to Patch ‘Leaky’ AI Ship
articles.content: When Pony Ma called Tencent Holdings Ltd.’s AI endeavor “a leaky ship” this summer, the billionaire founder sent ripples through a company that for years dominated the industry with WeChat. The social media and gaming leader was at the time struggling to catch the likes of DeepSeek in the post-ChatGPT age. One of his key lieutenants, Dowson Tong, came up with a surprising answer: let’s retool to focus on businesses.

articles.title: 小米米家金属旅行箱发售：无铆钉框体工艺、全新金属轴减重轮，1999 元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，小米米家金属旅行箱现已在京东发售，该产品主打无铆钉框体工艺，匹配全新金属轴减重轮，定价为 1999 元。京东小米米家金属旅行箱 1999 元直达链接IT之家注意到，新品箱体沿用米家行李箱标志性的横向条纹设计，箱体由高性能 6 系铝镁硅合金框体与 5 系铝镁合金箱壳组合而成，并采用无铆钉框体工艺。官方称，金属旅行箱制作流程复杂，对材质与工艺成熟度要求较高，整箱需经过约 150 道工序。米家称其与 HINOMOTO 联合研发了静音万向轮，内部采用金属独立减震结构，并宣称获得 SGS 静音轮认证。页面给出的实验室口径数据为：行走 72 公里后轮皮磨损小于 2 毫米，行走噪音低于 43 分贝；同时通过万向轮行走性能 6 倍国标检测。拉杆部分采用航空级 6 系铝镁硅合金，表面经高抛光处理，官方称经 18000 次抽拉后仍能保持顺滑，并通过 6 倍国标耐疲劳测试，支持四挡高度调节。收纳方面，官方标注容量约 37 升，称可满足 3 至 5 天中短途出行；内部采用双侧 U 型拉链封闭结构与双隔板设计，内衬为桃皮绒面料，并宣称具备抑菌特性。锁具采用一键中控式 TSA 密码锁，官方称按压一次即可同时打开两侧锁扣，便于安检与取物。细节配置上，产品配有锌合金防撞护角、慢回弹双料提手、超细纤维合成革拉杆握把、高亮质感合页与耐磨脚垫；官方同时宣称其通过拉杆耐疲劳 6 倍国标检测及整箱性能国标检测。京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 2026 年 11 月索尼 PS Plus 会免游戏公布：含《死亡岛 2》《古墓丽影 IV–VI：复刻版》等
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，索尼 2026 年 11 月 PlayStation Plus 一档会免游戏阵容现已正式公布，分别为《死亡岛 2》PS4/PS5 版、《古墓丽影 IV–VI：复刻版》PS4/PS5 版和《怪物列车 2》PS5 版，玩家可以在 11 月 3 日至 11 月 30 日领取。《死亡岛 2（Dead Island 2）》PSN 港服定价：398 港币（IT之家注：现汇率约合 338.9 元人民币）起游戏地址：点此访问《死亡岛 2》是由 Dambuster Studios 开发、Deep Silver 发行的一款第一人称动作角色扮演游戏，将惊悚的丧尸题材与美式黑色幽默完美融合。游戏舞台设定在经历致命病毒肆虐后被全面封锁的洛杉矶 —— 在游戏里被称为充满血腥与狂热的“地狱洛杉矶”（HELL-A）。玩家可以从六名性格迥异、背景独特的免疫者中选择自己的角色，在满城丧尸的末日废土中杀出一条血路，并揭开病毒爆发背后的黑暗真相。《古墓丽影 IV–VI：复刻版（Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered）》PSN 港服定价：238 港币（现汇率约合 202.7 元人民币）游戏地址：点此访问《古墓丽影 IV–VI：复刻版》是由 Aspyr 和 Crystal Dynamics 联手推出的一款经典动作冒险游戏合集，收录了劳拉 · 克劳馥探险生涯中极具转折意义的三部经典作品：《古墓丽影 IV：最后的启示》、《古墓丽影 V：历代记》以及《古墓丽影 VI：黑暗天使》。《怪物列车 2（Monster Train 2）》PSN 港服定价：198 港币（现汇率约合 168.6 元人民币）游戏地址：点此访问《怪物列车 2》是由 Shiny Shoe 开发、Big Fan Games 发行的备受赞誉的 Roguelike 卡牌构筑策略游戏《怪物列车》的震撼正统续作。前作凭借其独特的垂直三层车厢塔防机制在卡牌游戏界声名鹊起，而这款续作则在继承经典核心玩法的基础上，进行了全面而深度的系统升级与内容扩充，为玩家带来了更为烧脑且极具重复游玩价值的策略盛宴。

articles.title: 韩芯片创企 FuriosaAI 挑战英伟达：新一轮融资后估值翻两番至 29 亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，据彭博社 28 日报道，韩国 AI 芯片初创公司 FuriosaAI 完成新一轮融资，估值增至 29 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 193.74 亿元人民币），接近此前的 4 倍，为挑战英伟达等行业巨头增添了筹码。FuriosaAI 宣布，D 轮融资筹集 6.2 亿美元（现汇率约合 41.42 亿元人民币），投资方包括美国 Infinitum Partners。韩国国民成长基金投资 2.8 亿美元（现汇率约合 18.71 亿元人民币），海外投资者合计出资 1.1 亿美元（现汇率约合 7.35 亿元人民币），参与融资的还有杰里科资本、Worldline Capital、新加坡 QUDA Capital 和阿布扎比 NeoFort Holding 等机构。英伟达芯片主导着 AI 数据中心市场，投资者则在寻找能效更高的替代方案，重点是 AI 推理。随着 AI 需求增长带动用电量攀升，如何降低推理成本成为行业竞争的主要焦点之一。成立于 2017 年的 FuriosaAI 今年 1 月开始量产 RNGD 芯片，名称发音同英文单词“Renegade”。公司还与博通合作开发第三代 AI 加速器，面向大规模 AI 基础设施。FuriosaAI 希望通过减少芯片运行时耗电较高的数据传输，在英伟达占据主导地位的市场扩大份额。去年上一轮融资时，公司估值为 7.35 亿美元（现汇率约合 49.1 亿元人民币）。FuriosaAI 称，台积电今年为其生产 2 万颗 RNGD 加速器，计划 2027 年将产量提高至 4 万颗以上。三星 SDS、LG 集团和韩国 AI 初创公司 Upstage 均采用了 RNGD 芯片。Naver、韩国产业银行、DSC Investment、Nextrans 和 Kakao Investment 等老股东也参与了本轮融资。韩国进出口银行则首次直接投资初创企业，投资对象正是 FuriosaAI。

articles.title: 首次引入视觉理解，腾讯混元 Hy4 、Hy4 flash AI 模型即将发布
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，据科创板日报在腾讯全球数字生态大会上获悉，腾讯集团高级执行副总裁、云与智慧产业事业群 CEO 汤道生现场宣布，Hy4 即将发布。据介绍，相比 Hy4 preview，Hy4 实现了全面大幅提升，尤其强化了各类长程和真实生产力任务的能力，显著提升了思维链效率，并首次引入了视觉理解。此外，Hy4 flash 也会在近期发布，提供极致性价比的实用模型，在继承 Hy4 视觉、Agent 等强大能力的基础上，通过模型和产品的深度 Co-Design 高频进化。据IT之家此前报道，8 月 28 日，腾讯发布 Hy4 preview，总参数 770 B，激活参数 49 B，上下文长度 1M。官方当时曾表示，Hy4 preview 在模型尺寸、上下文长度、数据规模上都进行了显著的扩展，预训练和后训练的共同进步带来了智能水平的又一次巨大提升。

articles.title: vivo 启动 OriginOS 7 第二批公测招募：X200、iQOO 13 等 16 款机型在列
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，vivo 官方于今日启动 OriginOS 7 第二批公测招募，面向 X 系列、S 系列、iQOO 系列及平板产品线共 16 款机型开放尝鲜申请，用户可在指定窗口期内报名并按申请顺序分批收到升级推送。招募与推送节奏本次尝鲜招募时间为 2026 年 10 月 29 日 10:00 至 11 月 12 日 23:59，招募人数不限量。官方将按申请顺序分批推送：10 月 29 日 10:30 推送首批 5000 人，10 月 30 日推送 15000 人，10 月 31 日推送 50000 人，11 月 1 日推送 100000 人，11 月 2 日向全部已申请用户推送，11 月 3 日至 12 日期间申请的用户可在当天收到推送。适配机型及版本要求参与尝鲜的机型需先升级至指定基线版本，否则无法通过申请入口校验：X Fold3 Pro：16.2.18.6.W10.V000L1 及以上X Fold3：16.2.19.1.W10.V000L1 及以上X200 Ultra：16.0.20.8.W10.V000L1 及以上X200 Pro（含卫星通信版）：16.1.24.23.W10.V000L1、16.1.24.23.W10.V0103L7 及以上X200 Pro mini：16.1.12.40.W10.V000L1 及以上X200s：16.1.12.40.W10.V000L1 及以上X200：16.1.12.40.W10.V000L1 及以上S60：16.0.11.10.W10.V000L1 及以上S60 元气版：16.1.21.11.W10.V000L1 及以上vivo Pad5 Pro：16.1.12.1.W10.V000L1 及以上iQOO 13：16.1.19.11.W10.V000L1、16.1.19.11.W10.V0101L50 及以上iQOO Neo10 Pro+：16.1.21.7.W10.V000L1 及以上iQOO Neo10 Pro：16.1.18.8.W10.V000L1 及以上iQOO Neo10：16.1.17.10.W10.V000L1 及以上iQOO Pad5 Pro：16.1.12.1.W10.V000L1 及以上基线版本检测路径为「设置 > 系统管理与升级 > 系统升级」。申请入口与操作路径用户需先将设备升级至上述指定版本，随后依次进入「设置 > 系统管理与升级 > 系统升级 > 右上角两点 > 升级尝鲜」，在新版本尝鲜卡片中点击「查看详情」并按提示完成申请；当页面下方按钮显示「已加入本次尝鲜，尝鲜版本将分批推送」即代表申请成功。通过 vivo 官网 App 打开 vivo 社区的用户，可直接跳转至申请界面完成操作。问题反馈方式尝鲜过程中如遇异常，用户可打开 vivo 官网 App，底部进入「社区」，顶部切换至「圈子」，找到「玩机圈 > 升级尝鲜」圈子，点击右下角「+」号并选择「提问」发布问题。官方注意事项本次更新不会主动删除用户数据，但仍建议在升级前完整备份重要资料并确认备份可用。升级完成后建议进入 vivo 应用商店将所有第三方 App 更新至最新版本，以获得更好兼容性。本次为大版本更新，升级包体积较大，建议在 Wi-Fi 环境下操作，并保持设备电量充足，升级过程中不要进行其他操作。尝鲜版可能存在未发现的问题，若无法接受，可通过官方降级工具回退至 OriginOS 6，降级前务必备份个人数据；已升级至 OriginOS 7 尝鲜版的设备无法直接退出尝鲜，需先降级至 OriginOS 6 后再进入尝鲜界面退出。升级后系统会在后台进行深度优化，期间可能出现轻微发热、耗电增加、卡顿或充电变慢等情况，建议通过「设置 > 电池 > 省电管理 > 应用深度优化」执行优化，或静置熄屏充电约 2 小时以加快完成。部分第三方应用在新系统尝鲜阶段可能出现适配问题，可在「升级尝鲜」圈子反馈，等待后续系统或应用更新修复。撤销尝鲜申请后将无法及时收到后续新尝鲜版本推送，操作需谨慎。未在本次名单内的 vivo 与 iQOO 机型，可等待官方后续发布的升级公告。

articles.title: “太空观测大礼包”风云三号 H 星、四号 C 星数据产品发布，普通公众也能领取
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，据央视新闻报道，中国气象局国家卫星气象中心今日在湖南长沙举办的 2026 年风云卫星用户大会上，发布风云三号 H 星（FY-3H 星）、风云四号 C 星（FY-4C 星）两颗卫星的数据产品。据介绍，这份“太空观测大礼包”，普通公众也能领取。气象行业用户可通过卫星中心数据湖、卫星直收站、气象大数据云平台“天擎”及省级实时资料下载平台获取；公众用户也能在风云卫星遥感数据服务网及客户端，以及“风云看地球”和“风云此刻”微信小程序上使用。IT之家附两颗卫星介绍如下：FY-3H 星于 2025 年 9 月发射，星上搭载 9 台载荷，可通过光学与微波多仪器联合观测，对台风进行三维立体扫描，并进一步强化温室气体精细探测。此次发布的 FY-3H 星数据包括 9 类基础数据及 31 种定量产品，涵盖云辐射、大气参数、陆海表和空间天气等类别。FY-4C 星于 2025 年 12 月发射，搭载 6 台载荷，可获取高时空分辨率的天气系统演变图像、大气温湿度、云、闪电及太阳高分辨率图像等参数。此次发布的 FY-4C 星数据包括 6 类基础数据及 71 种定量产品。两颗卫星数据产品的发布，进一步增强了我国温室气体探测、数值天气预报、生态环境监测和空间天气监测预警能力，也为“妈祖”风云卫星 AI 工具箱再添“粮草”，为全民早期预警贡献力量。相关阅读：《风云四号 C 星发射成功，全球最强静止轨道气象卫星详解》《首批风云卫星极端天气 AI 模型发布，27 秒就能生成台风“体检报告”》

articles.title: 上海：拟依法有序推动自动驾驶技术在出租汽车行业的应用
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，近日，《上海市出租汽车条例》公开征求意见。其中提出，依法有序推动自动驾驶技术在出租汽车行业的安全应用。交通、公安等部门依法加强指导和服务。IT之家从《条例》获悉，其中提到，运用大数据、区块链、人工智能等现代信息技术，拓展开发应用场景，提升出租汽车服务与管理的数字化、智能化水平。推进出租汽车行业的绿色低碳转型，鼓励和支持新技术、新能源、新装备在出租汽车行业的创新应用。总量调控方面，其中提出，市交通部门根据经济社会发展情况、市场供需状况、道路通行条件等因素，编制出租汽车总量调控方案，并建立动态监测机制。出租汽车总量调控方案报市人民政府批准后实施。区人民政府可以根据实际需要，设置区域巡游出租车。区域巡游出租车数量纳入出租汽车总量调控范围。服务设施方面，市、区人民政府应当结合乘客出行需求和道路通行条件，统筹布局出租汽车停车点、候客站、巡游出租车营业站、网约车专用上客区域、充电桩等服务设施。有关单位应当按照规定建设、维护出租汽车服务设施，任何单位和个人不得违法占用。运价方面，其中提出，市发展改革、交通、市场监管、人力资源社会保障等部门建立网约车运价监测机制，综合运用成本调查、行政指导、执法监管等方式，规范网约车平台价格行为，维护市场价格秩序。巡游出租车运价实行政府指导价。网约车运价实行市场调节价，因维护公平竞争秩序和公共利益需要，可以设置运价参考区间或者根据有关规定实行政府指导价。网约车平台应当综合考虑市场供需、运营成本、驾驶员收入水平等因素，合理确定网约车计价规则；确定、调整计价规则，应当提前三十日报市发展改革、交通部门备案。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 29 日消息，国产 3A 游戏《影之刃零》现已正式发售，登陆 PS5 与 PC 平台，国区数字标准版售价 268 元，数字豪华版售价 328 元。PS5 实体光碟将于 2027 年推出。IT之家附游戏商品页（https://store.steampowered.com/app/4115450/%E5%BD%B1%E4%B9%8B%E5%88%83%E9%9B%B6/?l=chinese）。据IT之家了解，《影之刃零》由灵游坊自主研发发行，采用虚幻引擎 5 打造，定位黑暗武侠题材第三人称动作冒险与单机动作 RPG，把中国武术与蒸汽朋克融合为功夫朋克风格，美术深沉黑暗，主打快节奏高速战斗。在《影之刃零》中，玩家将化身心脏遭受重创的剑客，在仅余六十六天的生命里，逃亡于刀光剑影和腥风血雨之间，并粉碎一桩笼罩在整个武林上方的惊天阴谋。在失序末法的武林中以身证道，以命寻心。游戏战斗系统提供 30 余种主武器与 20 多门夺自败者的奇诡武装，连击流畅、易上手而难精通，借助全新动作捕捉逐帧还原真实技击，以电影化演绎呈现中国功夫。IGN 为本作给出了 9 分评价，认为本作是近年来最出色的动作游戏之一。在长达约 50 小时的体验中，战斗始终保持较高水准，BOSS 战也具有足够的吸引力。不过，IGN 同时指出，游戏的复仇故事相对保守，部分空气墙和技术问题也会影响体验。VGC 同样肯定了战斗设计。游戏允许玩家同时装备两种武器，并通过切换武器、招架和闪避应对不同敌人。各类 BOSS 拥有不同的攻击模式和战斗机制，玩家需要观察攻击规律，再寻找反击机会。不过，VGC 也指出，部分敌人的连续攻击速度过快，玩家有时会陷入连续按下招架键的状态，而不是精准判断每一次攻击的时机。

articles.title: 具身智能军备竞赛，胜负手在工程生态
articles.content: 开源工程底座 FluxVLA Engine 技术报告全解读。    作者丨邓哲敏    编辑丨齐铖湧                                                                                                       一个模型在论文中取得好成绩，距离它真正驱动机器人完成任务，还有多远？模型能否接入现有的数据与训练流程，推理速度能否跟上机器人的控制节奏，生成的动作能否连续、稳定地执行，实验结果又能否在不同机器人上得到验证——这些问题，未必能靠再提升几个百分点的模型成功率来解决。过去半年，AI科技评论（雷峰网）在与业内人士交流时发现，一些反复出现的工程问题正在消耗大量研发资源：不同模型的数据格式难以统一，训练和评测流程各自为政，仿真中的结果到了真机上未必成立；好不容易跑通一套流程，换个模型、换份数据或换台机器人，又可能需要重新适配。模型在不断迭代，工程积累却未必能随之沉淀。这让雷峰网想起深度学习的发展历程。2017 年，PyTorch 正式开源，此后，框架、工具链与开发者社区不断完善，研究者得以在更成熟的基础设施上开展实验，而不必每次从底层重新搭建环境。今天的具身智能虽然面临不同的技术挑战，但同样需要解决一个问题：如何让已有的研发成果更容易复用，让不同技术路线能够在统一的工程框架下协作。逐际动力开源的 FluxVLA Engine，试图从工程层面回应这一问题。它并非又一个争夺模型性能排名的 VLA 模型，而是一套面向具身智能研发的工程底座，贯通数据、训练、评测、推理与真机部署。10 月 22 日，FluxVLA Engine 完成重要更新。我们拆解了它的最新技术报告，并重点关注四个问题：不同架构的模型能否接入同一套研发体系？模型从仿真走向真机，需要跨过哪些工程障碍？真实交互经验如何低成本地回流到模型优化中？当同一套流程覆盖更多模型与机器人时，它究竟展示出了怎样的能力？01新模型请先登记一套工程底座是否真正有用，首先要看它能否接纳不同的模型。对具身智能来说，模型是迭代最快的。今天使用一种 VLA 架构，明天可能尝试另一种动作生成方式；同一团队也可能同时研究多个策略模型。如果每换一次模型，就要重新整理数据、编写评测代码、改造部署接口，那么此前积累的工程经验很难持续发挥价值。模型可以不断更换，但围绕数据、评测和部署建立起来的工程能力，不应该每次都从头再来。FluxVLA Engine 的做法，是通过统一配置与组件注册机制，把不同模型接入研发流程时需要处理的差异，尽可能收敛到明确的接口中。可以理解为一份统一的实验清单，加上一套可供调用的组件目录。配置文件负责声明一次实验需要使用什么模型、如何处理数据、怎样开展评测，以及通过什么接口进行部署。注册机制则将视觉骨干、动作头、训练运行器和机器人相关操作组件等分别组织起来。开发者可以按需组合已经适配的组件，而不必为每一种模型重新搭建整套工程流程。这并不意味着任何模型都能在不做适配的情况下直接运行。不同架构仍然可能需要各自的适配器、动作空间转换和归一化处理。真正的价值在于：把不可避免的差异放到可管理的组件层，让已经打通的公共流程能够继续复用。从技术报告来看，FluxVLA 已经将多种架构差异明显的策略纳入同一套研发与评测体系，包括采用自回归路线的 OpenVLA、采用 flow-matching 路线的 π0.5，以及 DiT4DiT、GR00T 等不同技术路线的模型。这意味着，统一工程框架不必以牺牲模型多样性为代价。FluxVLA 的模型接入并不局限于开放权重的模型。GPT-6 Astra 此前就以纯 API 的方式接入，同一套闭环评测，不提供权重、不参与训练，评测器照常跑完流程、留好证据。就在最新技术报告发布后两天，MiniMax-M3.1-Flash 成为继 GPT-6 Astra 之后第二个 checkpoint-free 的纯 API 推理策略，开箱即可在 LIBERO 与 RoboCasa GR1 上跑评测。数据层面也遵循同一套逻辑。不同机

articles.title: 华为群英传之刘睿：AI助手要告别聊天框，从“被动响应”走向“主动服务”
articles.content: 在商汤没做成的技术，登上了华为发布会。作者：李秋悦编辑：吴彤2022年6月，刘睿港中文博士毕业，赶上的却是一个“坏时候”。深度学习的高光已持续近十年，新突破越来越难；疫情之下，经济低迷，同届不少同学选择延期，再守一年实验室。刘睿没有等，他直接去了商汤。两个月后，Stable Diffusion发布；又过了三个月，ChatGPT引爆全球。刘睿毕业时以为正在退潮的世界，忽然换了一片海——商汤赖以生存的生意，为手机厂商定制算法、出售授权，开始松动；原本需要一个团队单独研发的算法，正被一个个基础模型收编。然后是2023年12月，汤晓鸥去世。“定海神针”突然离开，公司内部人心惶惶。刘睿也第一次认真想：汤老师不在了，商汤怎么办，自己怎么办。回头看，这个“坏时候”里埋着他此前人生的所有伏笔。2014年考入电子科技大学，他最初学光电子，很快觉得天地太窄；转入英才实验学院后，吴恩达的CS229让他迷上机器学习，李飞飞的CS231n把他领进深度学习和计算机视觉。2018年，他进入港中文MMLab，在王晓刚、李鸿升门下研究生成式模型——那正是几年后掀起巨浪的方向。从传统机器学习到深度学习，他几乎踩着AI最热闹的鼓点走完了求学路，却在毕业这年，听见鼓点停了。2024年，刘睿加入华为。这一次，他想换一种做技术的方式：不再把算法卖给客户，而是直接把它交到用户手里。此前在商汤未能立项的对话式修图，被他推上了2025年华为Mate 80的发布会；年底，小艺大模型应用实验室成立，刘睿出任首任主任，研究范围涵盖大语言模型、多模态智能、Agent与具身智能。做研究与做产品，在他手里第一次合流。也正是在这个时候，2022年那个“坏时候”显出了另一副面孔：如果他像同学一样延期一年、守在实验室里等风停，等来的不会是避风港，只会是又一场追赶。所谓坏时机，不过是旧浪退去、新浪未至的间隙——有人站在岸边等，有人先下了水。现在，刘睿关心的不再是追不追得上技术，而是另一个问题：模型能做的，和用户要的，之间还差什么。以下是雷峰网左林右狸频道与刘睿（华为小艺大型模型应用实验室创始主任）的对话，经编辑。01 articles.title: Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: I consider what it means for AI assistance to save time. I contrast a stopwatch view, on which time saved is whatever the clock records, with a ledger view, on which it is a counterfactual that has to be read next to the errors the work lets through, and I argue for the latter. The argument has four parts. I define a model-free pair of quantities, time saved and excess escaped defects, and one decision number built from them: the break-even defect cost. I give a baseline model of checking in which, until the model is good enough not to check, a calibrated worker's escaped-defect rate does not depend on how good the model is; checking time grows with the logarithm of the model's error rate; and over-trust buys minutes on the clock at a larger cost in total minutes. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36077v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. articles.content:

Abstract: Language model agents for clinical cohort curation should accommodate evolving eligibility criteria without repeatedly processing unchanged requirements. We introduce CohortFlow, a steerable agent that represents natural language corrections as localized updates to a structured cohort specification and reconciles them with a persistent execution graph. Explicitly recorded semantic dependencies enable affected computations to be selectively invalidated while preserving valid prior results. articles.title: Why and How to Do Science When AI Is Better at It: A Framework Grounded in Human Understanding and Direction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36116v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI begins to match or exceed human researchers at core scientific tasks, two questions become pressing: \emph{why} should humans keep doing science, and \emph{how} should they use AI when they do? This paper argues that the second can be answered only by answering the first. It holds that one indispensable aim of science is \emph{durable, collective human understanding of the world, pursued in service of human ends and values}. From this principle it derives a two-part test for when a research task can be delegated to AI. The first part, \emph{human understanding}, requires that the scientific community remain able to explain, defend and contest the resulting claims, and retain the skills to do so. The second, \emph{human direction}, requires that judgments about which questions matter and what findings mean stay with accountable humans. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36146v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Prompt optimization should improve the image a user receives without changing the scene the user requested. Yet stylistic rewriting can weaken object attributes and relations even when global text--image similarity remains high. We propose StruPO, a structure-aware prompt editor that uses a calibrated scene graph as a shared representation for policy conditioning and image-grounded supervision. The graph exposes what should be preserved, while deletion, reordering, and insertion provide a token-aligned way to modify the prompt. This turns structural feedback from an external critique into a training signal for a reusable editing policy. Learning from that signal requires handling both uncertain grounding and stochastic image generation. StruPO retains grounding confidence through smooth reward shaping and averages multiple images for each edit before computing group-relative advantages. articles.title: Don't Pick a Winner: Knowledge Conflicts Need a Prior, Not a Rule
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36169v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A retrieval-augmented language model answers from two sources, the retrieved context and its own knowledge, and the two disagree whenever the context is incomplete or wrong. Existing methods settle the disagreement with a rule fixed at design time: follow the context, amplify it in proportion to how far it moves the model, or trust the model's memory. Each rule is confidently wrong in some deployment. In a decision-theoretic model of two sources, the score of any fixed rule is linear in the share of reliable contexts while the best attainable score is convex, so every fixed rule is beaten wherever it is not exactly optimal; and a symmetric divergence between the two sources, the signal adaptive decoding uses, carries no information about which one is right. articles.content:

Abstract: We study time-to-arrival (TTA) in sports: the shortest plausible time a player needs to reach an arbitrary location on the pitch given their current kinematic state, estimated as the lower envelope of observed locomotion times. Rather than modeling space ownership through position density estimation or closed-form physics-based models, we cast TTA as a conditional quantile regression problem, estimating the lower quantile of locomotion time so the model learns a player's lower-envelope arrival time. articles.title: Skill Dreaming: Evolving Repository Skills through Pull Request Streams
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36188v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on reusable skills for complex software engineering tasks, making skill libraries essential for repository development and maintenance. However, repository-specific skills must evolve with changing code structures, implementation conventions, and maintenance requirements. Pull requests (PRs) provide a natural source of such knowledge by recording how repositories evolve through implementation and review. Meanwhile, new PRs must follow repository-specific implementation patterns, modify related components consistently, and ensure that existing tests continue to pass while adding coverage for new functionality. This creates a mutually reinforcing cycle: PRs provide knowledge for updating skills, while these skills improve future PRs, maintain repositories, and support further skill evolution. articles.title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36234v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Requirements engineering (RE) is foundational to systems engineering (SE), as requirement defects can propagate downstream and adversely affect development outcomes. Although large language models (LLMs) are promising for requirement quality assessment, prior work shows that off-the-shelf models miss a large share of expert-identified defects, perform unevenly across quality criteria, and vary across executions. This study investigates whether infusing expert-derived SE knowledge can improve LLM-based requirement quality evaluation beyond off-the-shelf capability. We present MARQ, a modular, LLM-agnostic prototype that supplements LLMs with a criterion-specific knowledge stack operationalizing INCOSE requirement quality criteria and evaluated against off-the-shelf baselines on an expert-labeled NASA requirement set using Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and the open-weight Gemma 3 12B, with 100 executions per model. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36239v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sequential recommendation models typically predict a user's next action from recent session interactions, which limits personalization when short-term signals are weak or ambiguous. Rather than assuming that incorporating longer-term history and community signals is universally beneficial, we study when it actually helps. articles.content:

Abstract: Machine learning models deployed behind query interfaces expose more than their predictions, because an adversary can use those predictions to rebuild the model itself. Model stealing attacks (MSAs) exploit this exposure by training a surrogate model that replicates the decision behavior of a target through black-box queries alone, without access to its parameters or training data. SNNs communicate through sparse, discrete spikes, and their outputs depend on membrane potentials that evolve over time rather than on a static mapping from input to output. This temporal mode of computation suggests that the decision behavior of an SNN may be harder to reconstruct from its responses. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36335v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well across many real-world tasks but remain prone to hallucination, limiting their reliability in domains such as biomedicine and healthcare, where answers must be grounded in established knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates this problem by incorporating external information, but often overlooks logical relationships and relies heavily on the LLM's own reasoning, which can compromise answer faithfulness. We propose OA-RAG, an agent that integrates formal reasoning with LLM reasoning, drawing on both the logical structure and informal annotations of domain ontologies. For each answer, OA-RAG reports the ontology observations used as evidence and a model-assessed grounding level (entailed, supported, related, or unrelated) that characterises the strength of that evidence. Abstract: Letting a language model take gradient steps on the text it is reading, known as dynamic evaluation, lowers its loss on the rest of the document. Abstract: Data stream classification under concept drift and class imbalance requires models to adapt continuously while maintaining strong minority-class performance. Abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs), which process both visual inputs and text queries, incur high inference costs due to the large number of visual tokens, making visual token pruning a natural approach for improving efficiency. Abstract: Activation steering is a popular approach for shifting LLM output toward a desired behavior, and increasingly for generating realistic synthetic data. Abstract: Individual fairness in machine learning requires that similar individuals receive similar predictions. We study local predictive consistency as a node-level relaxation of pairwise individual fairness, where each prediction is compared with a similarity-weighted average of predictions in its local neighborhood. Abstract: Quantization, pruning, and model merging are popular transformations applied to deployment-ready LLMs to improve efficiency and downstream performance. Recent work has shown that these transformations can introduce a security threat: an adversary can train a model that passes safety checks in its pre-transformed state, only turning malicious once it is transformed for deployment. Abstract: Boruta is a widely used method for selecting gene panels from RNA sequencing data, and its most used implementation recommends Random Forest trees of depth 3 to 7, an untested setting. We tested whether this setting changes which genes are selected, using pan-cancer data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (10,469 tumors, 33 cancer types) and breast cancer PAM50 subtyping (981 tumors, 5 subtypes). A leakage-free protocol fitted every label-dependent step inside training folds, measured every effect against seed-to-seed variation, and held out a locked test set per task. In pan-cancer data, shallow trees changed the selection far more than a new seed did: the top-500 overlap with unlimited-depth selections was 0.37 at depth 5, against 0.84 to 0.93 between seeds at depth 5 or unlimited depth. Shallow trees confirmed 3.5 times fewer genes, missed markers of large classes and produced less accurate 50-gene panels (balanced accuracy 0.809 vs 0.889).

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33331v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adversarial training remains one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, but its standard PGD-based training is computationally expensive because adversarial examples are generated for every training sample. Selective adversarial training reduces this cost by perturbing only a subset of samples. However, existing selective techniques typically rely on point-wise difficulty signals such as loss, entropy, margin, or gradients. We show that these point-wise criteria do not capture local instability in a sample's neighborhood. Motivated by this, we propose Augmentation-Guided Adversarial Training (AGAT), a selective adversarial training framework that uses augmentation-induced local variation to allocate samples with unstable neighborhoods for adversarial training. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training contextual masking systems for personally identifiable information (PII) requires examples distinguishing maskable from preservable mentions of one entity type, but privacy restrictions limit access to real data. Author-based augmentation (SPY) labels mentions unrelated to the author as non-PII, presuming a single data subject and overlooking others. On Korean documents from six domains, it yields ReCoPII-Ko, a corpus with relation, privacy, and MASK/KEEP annotations, which we validate. Abstract: System One decision models such as Jev answer structured questions in a single forward pass without generating text, offering fast and computationally efficient clinical decision support. We evaluate MedJev, an open System One model that runs locally on a laptop, across ten medical benchmarks spanning medical knowledge, diagnosis, and patient level prediction using MIMIC IV and MIMIC IV ED. We compare MedJev against zero shot LLM baselines, published GPT results, and supervised models. MedJev achieves accuracies of 72.5 percent on MedQA, 75.4 percent on USMLE, and 80.1 percent on NEJM, approaching published GPT 4 performance while maintaining well calibrated confidence estimates (ECE 0.028 to 0.063). On patient level tasks, MedJev achieves an AUROC of 0.926 for In Hospital Mortality, exceeding XGBoost (0.902), but underperforms supervised models on operational outcomes such as ED Triage Admission (0.745 vs. 0.809). articles.title: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36013v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36083v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in Generative AI have substantially improved financial sentiment analysis through post-trained financial large language models (LLMs). However, existing approaches remain confined to predicting the sentiment of each article in isolation and operate as black boxes, which limits contextual understanding and hinders deployment in high-stakes financial decision-making. To this end, we introduce FinLLM-KG, a model-agnostic framework that combines causal LLMs with a financial knowledge graph, in order to inject temporally grounded, company-level knowledge from SEC 10-K filings at inference time, without updating model weights. Within FinLLM-KG, context is supplied either as a natural-language company profile or as a small set of relevance-ranked factual triples. Abstract: Bengali, spoken by over 230 million people, remains severely under-resourced in spoken language research. Existing open Bengali ASR corpora are confined to short, read or crowd-sourced speech and lack speaker diarization and long-form audio.
  We present Lipi-Ghor, a large-scale weakly-supervised Bengali speech corpus comprising 885 hours of audio sourced from 998 YouTube videos across 596 unique channels, spanning 17 diverse domains including audiobooks, drama, religious sermons, news, and regional dialects. articles.title: Frankly Speaking: The Company Election Integrity Keeps in Congressional Communication
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36187v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Election integrity is a shared commitment in American politics, but Democrats and Republicans in Congress increasingly mean different things by it. Analyzing 10,420 congressional e-newsletters sent from 2010 to 2025, we examine how the two parties invoke election terms such as ``integrity,'' ``security,'' and ``fraud.'' Using diachronic word embeddings, which track semantic change through how words are used in context, we measure how differently each party uses each term, how much each party shifts, and whether they share nearest semantic neighbors. We show that members of Congress do not need different words to tell different stories about elections. They need only place those same words in different company. Across nearly every term and year, the two parties surround election-integrity vocabulary with entirely different words. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36353v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often answer ambiguous inputs as if they had a single intended meaning. This is problematic because input ambiguity is an upstream source of uncertainty: when a prompt admits multiple valid interpretations, the key question is whether the model should answer directly at all. Abstract: We present AK_QMUL's submissions to the ArGuard-2026 shared tasks on Arabic harmful-prompt detection: a binary safe/unsafe task (B1) and a seven-way harm-domain task (B2). Abstract: Homoglyph and invisible-character watermarks are edit-based watermarks. Instead of changing how a model generates text, they hide a signal in the text after it is written. Abstract: When a Large Language Model (LLM) is trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) on multiple tasks, a task's primary reward can gate auxiliary rewards such as a length reward: on a failing response, an auxiliary cannot exceed the primary. articles.content:

Abstract: A major challenge facing AI scientific discovery pipelines is how to determine when a generated idea is meaningfully novel. Abstract: Written transcripts of the same speech can differ in ways that are not uniquely determined by the speech signal. Abstract: Multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) has achieved rapid progress with large-scale pretrained models and multilingual speech corpora. Abstract: Emergent generative AI technologies, while remarkably beneficial across several tasks and domains, can suffer from unforeseen vulnerabilities and difficult-to-anticipate failure modes. We show that when VLMs are requested to transform human face images to reflect race identities (e.g., Hispanic, Black, White, or Asian) and sexual orientation (e.g., gay or straight), VLMs often comply with such requests. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36022v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. We study this problem from two perspectives: geometric supervision during training and explicit geometric evidence during inference. Abstract: Geometry foundation models recover camera poses and dense geometry from a set of images with a feed-forward network, but they expect pinhole images. Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has rapidly become the preferred representation for high-fidelity novel view synthesis and 3D scene reconstruction. However, the learned representation encodes sensitive visual information including human faces, license plates, documents, and computer screens, raising significant privacy concerns when trained splats are shared or deployed. In this work, we address the underexplored problem of privacy preservation in Gaussian Splatting by proposing a representation-level anonymization framework that directly anonymizes a trained splat. Given a trained splat and a user-provided reference view identifying sensitive content, our method localizes the corresponding regions in the underlying 3D representation and directly anonymizes them, ensuring that the sensitive information is absent from all subsequently rendered novel views while preserving the overall scene geometry and visual fidelity. Abstract: Learning velocity fields directly in pixel space is difficult and slow. We show that coarse second-order image statistics can ease this task: frozen Wiener estimates improve velocity learning, with gains extending beyond the linear predictions they explicitly provide. Moreover, we observe similar but complementary gains from frozen bases and pixel decoding. These observations motivate Wiener-informed Decoding (WiD), which uses statistical knowledge both for direct prediction and to organize decoder computation without modifying native blocks. WiD combines a trainable Wiener prediction path with coefficient interfaces that inject features into the native decoder and return its predicted coefficient corrections, with these components initialized with data statistics. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36195v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite rapid progress in visual understanding and document transcription, modern vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with a fundamental accessibility task: reading Braille from images. We introduce BrailleBench, a manually curated benchmark of 259 real-world Grade-1 and Grade-2 Braille images. We evaluate proprietary, open-weight, OCR-specialized, and tool-assisted multimodal systems and find that standalone general-purpose models perform poorly at directly transcribing Braille images, whereas tool-assisted systems perform much better. We design a synthetic Braille generation pipeline with diverse layouts and image perturbations. A 2B VLM model trained on our synthetic data reaches 87% exact match on Grade-1 and 61% on Grade-2 BrailleBench, outperforming standalone VLMs and achieving the highest Grade-2 exact match score among the evaluated systems. Abstract: Monocular 3D human mesh recovery (HMR) remains unreliable under weak observations caused by long camera-to-person distances, occlusion, and motion blur. In challenging scenarios such as sports, these factors make the problem highly ambiguous, as different 3D poses may yield similar 2D projections. This ambiguity is especially severe for one-stage HMR, which recovers all meshes directly from the full image without person crops or external 2D cues. To handle this ambiguity, we present UT-HMR ( Uncertainty-guided Temporal HMR), to our knowledge the first one-stage HMR framework to capture correlated pose uncertainty across joints. Abstract: Long-video question answering is challenging since the answer often hinges on a few decisive moments scattered throughout the video, while memory constraints force Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to sample frames at extremely low rates, resulting in sparsity that risks omitting key evidence. Though aggressively enlarging the context size is intuitive, we argue that performance remains fundamentally constrained by the bias, \emph{i.e.}, the misleading cues caused by spurious \textit{linguistic} correlations and salient yet irrelevant \textit{visual} observations. Abstract: Dyadic relationship recognition aims to identify the latent social relationship between two individuals from their multimodal interactions. Existing methods typically project heterogeneous cues into a shared representation and optimise a flat classification objective, overlooking that relationships may rely on different interaction patterns. For instance, distant relationships can often be inferred from direct behavioural correspondence, whereas close relationships are better reflected by coordinated affective, behavioural, and multimodal responses. To address this limitation, we propose HiRe-DRR, a Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning framework that organises relationship evidence from three complementary perspectives: feature level, interaction type, and relationship hierarchy. Abstract: Are concepts and mechanisms unified across modalities in current AI models, or instead implemented separately for each one? Our study goes beyond simple correlational alignment (e.g. representational similarity) because steering is fundamentally causal. We study cross-modal steering in several unified multimodal models (UMMs), since they possess shared parameters for language and image generation, focusing on these two modalities. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36327v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video Large Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in video understanding and reasoning, but processing long visual sequences incurs substantial computational, latency, and memory overhead. This survey examines training-free inference acceleration, focusing on reducing inference costs while preserving task-relevant spatiotemporal evidence. We organize existing methods by their intervention stages in the inference pipeline, covering input, visual encoding, projector, prefill, and decoding. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is discussed separately as a cross-stage extension with varying calibration requirements. We analyze how intervention position affects evidence preservation and computational savings, and why local efficiency improvements may not translate into end-to-end acceleration. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36337v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-task learning (MTL) improves model efficiency by sharing representations across related vision tasks, but it often suffers from negative transfer when task updates interfere with one another. Existing conflict-mitigation methods typically operate in gradient space, requiring explicit task-gradient manipulation and additional optimization steps. We propose Conflict-Resolution through Low-Rank Matrices for Multi-Task Learning (CRLoMTL), a parameter-efficient framework that mitigates task interference in the low-rank parameter-update space. CRLoMTL learns task-specific LoRA updates through task-specific passes, where each task updates its own low-rank matrices, and integrates these updates through global shared-subspace fusion. Abstract: We tackle the challenge of building real-time interactive video worlds with user-defined behaviors. Yet existing end-to-end video world models typically learn interaction dynamics within the generator, making it difficult to specify object-level rules and reason about their consequences. Given user-specified rules, a coding agent creates a Box World Engine that determines interaction outcomes and exposes the resulting object states through a lightweight interface of layout boxes, persistent object attributes, and dynamic status variables, leaving appearance and physical effects to generative rendering. Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise for breast imaging, but limited labeled data, institutional data fragmentation, and privacy concerns hinder centralized training. We investigate a privacy-aware federated learning framework combining pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with client-level differential privacy. We compare general-purpose CLIP models, biomedical BiomedCLIP, and an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 baseline on two public breast imaging datasets, with and without differential privacy. Abstract: Perceiving human body motion is critical for multimodal systems that understand and assist people. Yet current evaluations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) largely focus on objects, scenes, and coarse actions, leaving their ability to reason about the body itself poorly assessed. This is especially challenging from the egocentric perspective, in which the body is only partially visible and motion must be inferred from occluded and temporally distributed cues. Abstract: We present Scalable Pixel-anchored End-to-end Diffusion (SpeeDiff), a latent diffusion method that jointly trains the VAE and the diffusion model from scratch. In principle, joint training allows the diffusion loss gradient to directly guide the VAE encoder, encouraging the formation of a generation-friendly latent space and potentially yielding faster convergence than the conventional two-stage approach with a pretrained frozen VAE. However, a naive end-to-end implementation severely degrades performance, as unrestricted backpropagation of the diffusion loss leads to latent space collapse. Abstract: World-action models (WAMs) offer a promising framework for embodied intelligence, yet mainstream approaches remain centered on video foundation models or vision-language models. Abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. Abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has predominantly relied on open-loop imitation learning for training, which presents two limitations. First, expert demonstrations show only one behavior per scenario, so the model cannot learn alternative valid behaviors and, in turn, cannot adapt to user-specified preferences at test time. Second, noise or ambiguity in these demonstrations can produce inconsistent, unreliable supervision for the end-to-end models. Driving is inherently multi-modal: multiple different behaviors can be valid responses to the same scene, and this diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. We introduce a planning paradigm that learns the path through imitation while scoring a set of candidate speeds across multiple criteria with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints. articles.title: Program-Level Adversarial Co-Adaptive Self-Play for Robotic Security
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36143v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents can adapt robotic software by revising executable programs, but successful responses to an evolving opponent may not remain effective. We present a framework for program-level adversarial co-adaptive self-play in which coding agents generate attacks and defenses from tested opponent code and mission feedback, without model fine-tuning. Environment-specific interfaces support external programs for autonomous driving and SDK-level defenses for humanoid locomotion. Two eight-generation case studies reveal concrete software responses: a driving defender introduces direct-actuation recovery, while a humanoid defender revises incoming-state validation. These responses provide local task recovery but do not establish sustained robustness. The framework makes such adaptation and limitations observable through executable artifacts and task-level evidence.

articles.title: ASPEN: Adaptive Semantic Reasoning via Command Persistence Prediction for Efficient Navigation VLAs
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36285v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Navigation vision-language-action (VLA) policies repeatedly invoke costly semantic reasoning even when the next command remains unchanged. Command reuse can reduce computation but risks missing instruction-dependent turns or stops. We introduce ASPEN, an event-triggered scheduler based on command persistence prediction: estimating whether the frozen base policy would reissue its previous command. A lightweight multimodal predictor combines temporal observations, language instructions, execution history, and cached VLA confidence. At eligible command boundaries, sufficient predicted persistence permits command reuse. Otherwise, ASPEN triggers fresh semantic reasoning from the VLA. Evaluated with frozen NaVILA on cross-dataset RxR-CE val-unseen, ASPEN reduces VLA calls by 9.5% and estimated inference time by 8.1%, including scheduling overhead. It maintains comparable navigation performance and preserves identical baseline action sequences

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36407v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: TrackJoint is a Modelica MultiBody component that turns a three-dimensional road surface into a joint with two degrees of freedom. The two joint coordinates are the distance travelled along a reference line and the sideways offset from that line. Together they give the position, orientation and angular velocity of a single frame_b connector. All road geometry reaches the joint as a small set of periodic piecewise-quintic splines, so one component can represent any circuit whose splines have been fitted beforehand. The road constraint is closed with d'Alembert's principle. The two generalized forces that belong to the joint coordinates are set to zero, so no Lagrange multipliers are needed. The joint is connected to a multibody race car in Dymola and the pair is exported as one FMI~3.0 FMU. The same FMU is then used for time-domain simulation and for CasADi/IPOPT minimum lap-time optimization, with no change to the model in between. This

articles.title: A Singularity Avoiding Track Model for Race Car Optimization
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36430v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A track fitting pipeline is presented that converts a measured racetrack point cloud into a closed, $C^4$ differentiable, three-dimensional surface model suitable for high-fidelity Modelica race-car optimization. The surface is a Monge patch, parametrised by a curvilinear arc-length coordinate measured along the minimum-curvature line (MCL) and a signed lateral offset, with a height polynomial of user-selectable degree capturing the cross-sectional elevation profile. The choice of MCL as the reference line is deliberate since anchoring the same surface on the geometric centre-line can cause adjacent normals to cross inside the drivable region on tight corners. The resulting non-injective parametrisation assigns multiple curvilinear addresses to the same three-dimensional point and returns invalid road geometry. articles.title: Ground Sample Distance Constrained k-Coverage Viewpoint Planning via Set Multi-Cover Formulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36450v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Drone-based 3D reconstruction and inspection require viewpoints that satisfy image-quality constraints while observing each surface region multiple times, which overlap-based planning heuristics do not guarantee. We study ground sample distance (GSD)-constrained $k$-coverage viewpoint selection for structures represented by surface voxels. Candidate viewpoints are generated along outward surface directions, screened with distance, viewing-angle, field-of-view, and occlusion tests, and augmented for voxels with insufficient visibility. Selection is then posed as set multi-cover with per-voxel coverage demands. We propose a dynamically weighted greedy heuristic that prioritizes remaining coverage deficits and scarce viewing alternatives, and compare it with sequential overlap-based pruning and an integer linear programming (ILP) formulation on the same candidate pools. articles.title: Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Stochastic Motion Tokenization
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36452v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While velocity-commanded RL policies are effective for controlling quadrupeds, they are a limited interface for humanoids that need to perform complex whole-body motions. Furthermore, RL tracking policies for whole-body motions typically have limited information about the desired future motion, preventing them from performing controlled deviations to achieve long-term task success; such information is particularly relevant when a controller must prepare for transitions between behaviors. We address these challenges using concise motion representations that can be generated by a high-level controller, given a behavior label or text command. articles.title: SVIn+: Multi-Modal Framework for Robust Underwater State Estimation using 3D Sonar, Visual-Inertial, Water-Pressure, and DVL
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36454v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. A fundamental challenge in any autonomous underwater operation, from control to safe navigation and mapping, is state estimation; a notorious hard problem to address, especially in low visibility conditions. In this paper, we tackle this problem, by presenting SVIn+, a multi-sensor framework for robust state estimation of AUVs equipped with an IMU, cameras, a water-pressure sensor, a Doppler Velocity Log (DVL), and a compact 3D sonar. articles.title: GRAFT: Geometry-Aware Residual Adaptation for Foundation Trackers
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) provide reusable whole-body motion priors: given a kinematic reference, they generate coordinated joint commands for motion replay, teleoperation, and VLA control. However, trained primarily on flat-ground motion, BFMs lack an explicit mechanism to adapt foot placement, swing clearance, and contact timing to local terrain. Many terrain-aware BFM approaches address this limitation by retraining or fine-tuning the tracker together with perception, incurring substantial data and computation costs while coupling ordinary tracking to the perception pathway. To bridge this gap, we propose GRAFT, a geometry-aware residual adaptation framework for frozen behavior trackers. GRAFT preserves the BFM parameters and motion-reference interface, while a lightweight adapter adds terrain-conditioned corrections only to lower-body execution targets. articles.title: RoboAuto: Autonomous Robot Program Search through Multi-Level Physical Understanding
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36533v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recently, LLM-based autonomous agents have shown strong capabilities in iteratively generating, evaluating, and refining executable solutions. In robotic manipulation, Code-as-Policy lets these agents search over modular and editable robot programs. However, effective program search requires physical understanding: agents must understand how objects can be manipulated, how scene geometry constrains actions, and why interactions succeed or fail. Existing methods rely mainly on execution feedback for program refinement, often leaving these physical questions unresolved. We introduce RoboAuto, a framework for robot program search that explicitly organizes physical understanding at the object, scene, and interaction levels through three components. articles.title: A generalist policy for muscle-driven control across individual musculoskeletal models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36535v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Differences in musculoskeletal morphology challenge policy reuse across individual models. Here we present MyoAcross, a framework that combines individual musculoskeletal model construction, morphology-conditioned policy learning and virtual model augmentation to enable muscle-driven reference-motion tracking without individual fine-tuning. Across 31 held-out individual models, MyoAcross achieves 99.24% completion and reduces tracking error by 22.60% relative to an unconditioned multilayer perceptron. Policy reuse extends to models of 22 held-out individuals constructed from single-image shape estimates, measured height and body mass, and, with asymmetry augmentation, to models with unilateral lower-limb shortening. Comparisons with measurements from 120 additional individuals show agreement in vertical ground reaction force waveforms and channel-dependent agreement between simulated muscle activations and electromyography. articles.title: A Trainable CPG Framework for Quadruped Locomotion
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36537v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present CPG-ENN, a trainable quadruped locomotion framework that combines explicit neural coordination with learned motion realization. A symmetry-based eight-neuron central pattern generator (CPG) supplies gait rhythms, while a pretrained, leg-shared execution neural network (ENN) maps rhythmic signals and trajectory parameters to joint-angle references without online inverse kinematics. A single feedback policy modulates six physically interpretable trajectory variables. The controller tracks planar velocity and yaw-rate commands across walk, trot, pace, bound, and pronk without gait-specific learned controllers or transitionspecific rewards. Simulation yields 99.39% transition success across all 20 directed gait pairs and all source-target speed combinations from {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0} m/s. articles.title: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36539v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans are dexterous, but traditional data collection paradigms such as teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and wearable exoskeletons force humans to act through the robot embodiment, bottlenecking their dexterity. Retargeting can avoid this. However, existing methods purely translate kinematics and ignore the real-world contact dynamics essential for task success. We present CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation, a simulator and object-free framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions by explicitly preserving contact force targets. CARD unifies human data sources including video, motion capture, and tactile gloves via a shared hand--contact representation and generates explicit contact force targets in addition to kinematics. articles.title: REACH: An RL-based Hierarchical Humanoid Crawling Framework for Adaptable Confined Space Traversal
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36546v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humanoid locomotion in confined spaces requires continuous height adaptation across multiple locomotion modes, yet most existing approaches remain limited to height-adjustable bipedal walking. We present REACH, an RL-based hierarchical framework that enables a Unitree G1 humanoid to traverse height-constrained environments through variable-height bipedal walking and crawling. The learned policies regulate body height over complementary command ranges of 1.27--0.50m in bipedal locomotion and 0.50--0.20m in crawling, extending traversal beyond the clearance limits of crouched walking. To address contact-rich crawling dynamics, we employ a history-conditioned latent representation that captures terrain and interaction context from proprioceptive observations. articles.title: AI做中学 创未来｜智源SoulAgent持续拓展教育应用
articles.content: 10月19日至24日，北京智源人工智能研究院（以下简称“智源研究院”）连续走进中国人民大学附属中学，先后支持北京市“做中学”领航行动海淀区工作部署会暨科学与工程实践研讨会、“AI做中学，创未来——人工智能赋能创新人才培养研讨会”等活动，围绕SoulAgent在真实课堂、教研和学习场景中的应用开展实践与交流。 SoulAgent是智源研究院推出的“越用越懂你的个人智能体”。在教育场景中，SoulAgent围绕“帮我听课”、教师AI分身、作文批改、教学答疑等方向，探索AI如何帮助教师提升教学效率、沉淀教学内容，同时通过反馈、追问等方式支持学生理解问题、拓展思路、持续思考。 图注：SoulAgent走进校园，围绕真实教学与学习场景开展应用实践。 “帮我听课”：同时听多堂课，让课堂内容持续服务教研公开课、听课和教研等场景中，多门课程往往同时进行，教师既需要关注课堂现场，也要记录内容、梳理重点并完成课后复盘，有限的时间很难兼顾所有感兴趣的课程。SoulAgent“帮我听课”通过AI速记、智能总结和持续问答，辅助记录课堂内容、梳理教学重点。即使无法进入每一间课堂，教师也可以在课后回顾感兴趣的课程，并围绕课堂内容继续提问，让“听课”不再受限于同一时间只能进入一间教室。 10月21日活动期间，27节公开课接入SoulAgent“帮我听课”，通过课堂文字整理、教学要点梳理等功能，为教师回顾课堂、开展教学复盘提供参考。当天上午多门研究课并行开展，下午随即进入7个教研分论坛，沉淀下来的课堂速记和总结也可以成为后续讨论的共同参考，减少对课堂内容的重复回顾，把更多时间用于教学分析、经验交流和深入研讨。 从课堂记录到课后追问，再到教学复盘和教研交流，SoulAgent希望让一次性的课堂内容进一步沉淀为可查询、可回顾、可持续使用的教学资源。  图注：SoulAgent通过课堂文字整理、教学要点梳理和持续问答，为教师回顾课堂和开展教学复盘提供参考。教师AI分身：让AI先理解教师，再辅助教学如果说“帮我听课”解决的是课堂信息如何被更高效地记录和使用，那么教师AI分身进一步面对的，是AI如何真正适应不同教师的教学方式。 不同教师有自己的课程设计、评价尺度、批注习惯和讲评重点，真实教学并不存在一套完全统一的标准。SoulAgent将教师的课程资料、评价标准、批注样例、讲评口径以及实际使用中的反馈持续沉淀，形成专属教师分身。在此基础上，教师AI分身可以按照具体教师的专业标准，辅助完成作文批改、课堂总结、教学答疑等任务，并在持续使用中逐步贴近教师本人的评价尺度和教学方式。 因此，教师AI分身并不是为所有教师提供同一套“标准答案”，而是将教师自己的知识、经验和专业标准沉淀下来，让AI先理解教师，再按照教师的要求提供辅助。   从教师AI分身到英语作文批改，进入真实教学任务在英语作文批改场景中，教师提供评分标准、批注样例、讲评材料等专业依据，SoulAgent教师AI分身将这些教学标准带入具体批改任务，一个班级的个性化批改报告可以快速生成。 在实际应用中，SoulAgent教师AI分身可以根据具体教学需求，为学生提供更有针对性的修改建议，同时辅助教师梳理班级共性问题、典型案例和改进方向，并将有价值的内容持续沉淀，用于后续讲评、备课和教学。 对学生而言，反馈从一个分数进一步走向具体的问题分析和修改建议；对教师而言，可以减少部分重复性的分析整理工作，把更多时间投入课堂讲评和个别指导；对于教研而言，则可以基于真实教学数据更加系统地发现共性问题和教学重点。 图注：SoulAgent教师AI分身结合教师专业标准，为作文批改、课堂讲评和后续教学提供辅助。 走进校园现场，与一线师生面对面交流两次活动期间，不同学科教师结合课堂记录、备课、作业反馈、教学答疑等实际任务了解和体验SoulAgent，学生也围绕知识问答、课后学习和持续追问等场景进行互动。通过问卷、共创墙和面对面交流，师生分享了对AI辅助教学与学习的实际感受和期待。从帮助教师提升教学效率，到为学生提供更具体的反馈和持续追问支持，AI的价值正在从“更快完成任务”进一步走向“更好支持思考”：让教师把更多专业时间投入教学设计与学生指导，也让学生把更多注意力投入理解、判断和深入思考。  图注：师生围绕SoulAgent教育应用进行现场体验与交流。 未来，智源研究院将继续与中国人民大学附属中学在教育领域深化合作，围绕真实课堂、教研和学习场景持续探索AI教育应用。同时，SoulAgent也将进一步拓展教育、会议智能服务、专家分身等更多应用方向，让“越用越

articles.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
articles.content: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53-7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31 times faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives.

articles.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

articles.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
articles.content: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. However, quantization error is widely assumed to cause unavoidable semantic loss, fundamentally limiting the semantic fidelity of discrete visual tokens and positioning continuous visual representations as an intrinsic upper bound. Using multimodal understanding as a proxy for semantic fidelity, we revisit this assumption and find quantization error unreliable, as discrete representations with substantially larger errors can achieve better understanding. Instead, the effective bit budget of discrete indices emerges as a key determinant of downstream performance. However, existing quantizers eventually saturate as additional codebooks contribute progressively less semantic information. As one approach to alleviating this saturation, we introduce Factorized Vector Quantization, which quantizes complementary, fixed-dimensional views of the visual feature with symmetric parallel codebooks. It continues to improve at larger bit budgets, ultimately matching continuous visual representations in multimodal understanding. Trained on industrial-scale multimodal data, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance among discrete-representation models, outperforming UniAR and Emu3-Chat by 22.8% and 59.2%, respectively, on a nine-metric average. To our knowledge, it is also the first discrete-representation model competitive with strong continuous-representation models such as Qwen3-VL, including on fine-grained OCR tasks. We further identify the key principles and a practical recipe enabling this competitiveness. These results and insights support the potential of discrete visual representations to underpin large-scale native multimodal foundation models. Code and models are available at https://github.com/hustvl/FVQ

articles.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
articles.content: Test-time adaptation helps a deployed model respond to changing inputs, but the same intervention can rescue one batch and damage the next. Updating normalization statistics, for example, can improve corrupted images yet fail when a batch contains mostly one class. Average accuracy hides these failures and cannot tell a model when to use an intervention. Target labels can guide this decision, but they are scarce and some choices are already clear. We introduce PORTAL, a controller that chooses when to deploy an intervention, which inputs to label, and when to stop querying. Each available prediction rule is a candidate, and its predictions are fixed before current feedback arrives. Every acquired label therefore evaluates all candidates on the same input. PORTAL combines these shared comparisons and directs queries toward candidates that can still overtake the current leader. It stops when the remaining labels cannot change the choice or when the possible accuracy gain no longer justifies another query. Our analysis links the required feedback to accuracy gaps and shared mistakes, explaining why some choices need much less evidence. Experiments show that this control turns an intervention that loses accuracy overall into a useful choice on selected batches. It prevents severe failures caused by changes in arrival order and preserves gains across complete corruption streams. When a fixed rule already works well, PORTAL uses little feedback to retain its performance. Periodic label checks reveal when past evidence needs refreshing and help the controller recover as conditions change. The acquired labels also train stronger candidates for future batches, and selection brings nearly all of their accuracy gains into deployment. The same feedback therefore improves both the choice made now and the predictions available to later batches.

articles.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
articles.content: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. We evaluate HoS on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B. We compare it against SecAlign++, a state-of-the-art finetuning-based defense, and ASIDE, a defense that, like ours, builds instruction-data separation into the model architecture. We show that HoS offers greater robustness to adaptive attacks, better performance on standard utility benchmarks, and matches top performance on standard agentic prompt injection benchmarks. More specifically, the black-box RL-Hammer attack reaches 97% ASR against GPT-OSS-20B and 85% against SecAlign, but only 10% against HoS. Claudini, a state-of-the-art white-box attack, strengthened against HoS through autoresearch, requires 3 times more FLOPs to reach the same ASR on HoS as it does on GPT-OSS-20B or SecAlign. HoS preserves base-model utility across standard multiple-choice benchmarks and prompting setups, whereas SecAlign and ASIDE degrade in few-shot settings. On agentic benchmarks with static attacks, HoS and SecAlign perform similarly and substantially improve the security-utility trade-off over the base model. ASIDE struggles with tool use, achieving only 10% utility. These results show that prompt injection robustness can be achieved and improved through targeted attention interventions.

articles.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
articles.content: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = Ψ(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $Ψ$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

articles.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
articles.content: Atmospheric chemical mechanisms are commonly distributed in the language of the Kinetic PreProcessor (KPP), which generates efficient Fortran or C code but does not fit into the differentiable programming frameworks in which machine-learning models are developed. We present KPPax, a kinetic preprocessor that generates differentiable, just-in-time compiled, and vectorisable chemistry code in JAX from mechanisms written in the KPP language. KPPax evaluates the rate law with sparse operations in log space, which keeps it differentiable, and integrates the stiff system with the implicit solvers and the forward- and reverse-mode adjoints of the \texttt{diffrax} library, so that exact sensitivities are obtained without hand-derived adjoint code. We demonstrate two applications with the POLLU benchmark mechanism. In the first, the Fisher information matrix computed from an automatically differentiated Jacobian predicts, before any fit, which of the 25 rate coefficients a flow-tube-like design can identify, and noisy synthetic estimation confirms the predicted uncertainties of the nine identifiable rate coefficients to within about 30\% while revealing clusters of fast reactions of which only ratios are constrained. In the second, a neural-network correction of an emission inventory is trained offline on per-scenario 4D-Var retrievals and then fine-tuned online through the chemical model, which reduces the error of the biogenic correction by a factor of 2.4--5 and recovers information on low-temperature emissions that the individual retrievals lose. KPPax makes KPP mechanisms directly usable for parameter estimation and hybrid physics--machine-learning modelling.

articles.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
articles.content: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals. We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum. With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust. On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops. In 13.3 hours of real-robot evaluation over 4,800 unseen goals across 4 objects and diverse wrist orientations, the state-based policy reaches 95.2% of goals within 2 cm and 0.4 rad, and the filter cuts its drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals. The policies can also spin a lightbulb held in an arbitrary pose, reach out-of-distribution goals, withstand fast arm motion and perturbations, and, needing only a wrist camera, serve as portable skills such as screwing in a lightbulb. We release the full recipe as a platform for studying performance, reliability, and safety in high-dimensional dexterous systems. Videos and more are available at https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/.

articles.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
articles.content: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the prompt optimizer to select which agent experiences should shape prompt optimization. In particular, GEPA-Curator consists of two components: task curation, which filters out tasks that are likely to provide noisy or unreliable learning signals, and prior success retrieval, which selectively retrieves past successful trajectories for a task and provides them as additional context to the prompt optimizer. We evaluate GEPA-Curator on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and $τ$-bench, using both Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. GEPA-Curator matches or exceeds the mean performance of both baselines, with gains of up to 20.7% over GEPA and 21.2% over ACE.

articles.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
articles.content: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.

articles.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
articles.content: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents. To do so, we propose the SynthAPI pipeline, which explicitly controls the diversity of generated environments along the axes of tools, tasks, and the databases on which the tools operate. By systematically varying SynthAPI's generation controls in 458,752 tasks across 849 trained models of four different sizes, we derive a scaling law that predicts downstream tool-use agent generalization based on the scale and composition of the synthesized environments. These predictable relationships reveal several lessons for scaling tool-use agent data. As data budgets grow, scaling tool and database diversity becomes more effective than increasing the number of tasks, and increasing data complexity yields larger gains. Scaling according to these findings yields agents that outperform models trained on data from prior work in large-scale tool-use agent and synthetic environment generation across four evaluation benchmarks.
